title: Enablement Controls and Authorization Patterns (Company-wide)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook defines the standard controls, decision patterns, and lightweight templates used across Redwood for: access & permissions, change management, data governance, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel policy enforcement. The intent is to provide a single, pragmatic reference that teams can adapt while maintaining company-wide consistency and auditability.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time employees (FTEs), contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or who incur business expenses on Redwood’s behalf.
- Operational owners must follow the patterns below when designing team-specific processes; deviations require a documented exception and approval from People Ops and Security.

Ownership and Stewardship
- People Ops: primary owner for access lifecycle policies, travel and expenses templates, and approval matrices.
- Security: owner for privilege classification, RBAC design patterns, and sensitive-data handling rules.
- Finance & Procurement: owners for supplier selection policy, PO thresholds, and expense reconciliation.
- Team Leads: owners for day-to-day approvals (team-level access, change windows) and local adoption.

1) Access & Permissions (Authorization Patterns)
- Principle: least privilege by default, time-bound elevated access, and justification for cross-team role grants.
- Roles & Role Templates: teams should base role definitions on the company Role Template Catalog (examples below). Each template must include: allowed resources, typical justification examples, escalation path, and default TTL (time-to-live).

  Example role template (text table):
  | Role name | Permission scope | Default TTL | Approver | Justification examples |
  | Engineers/read-only | Prod read across services | 90 days | Team lead | Debugging incidents, audits |
  | Oncall/write | Deploy/infra runbooks | 30 days | SRE manager | Incident mitigation, emergency config |

- Access Request Flow (standardized):
  1. Requestor files an access request via the Access Portal (link: /internal/access-portal). Include reason, duration, and any resources.
  2. Auto-check: system verifies no policy conflict and annotates required approvals.
  3. Primary approver (team lead) approves or denies within 48 hours.
  4. If sensitive scope (see classification below), Security review is required before grant.
  5. Provisioning executes with TTL; reminders at 7 and 2 days prior to expiry.

- Temporary Elevated Access (Breakglass):
  - Breakglass requests must be submitted with incident id and post-hoc justification. Emergency access is time-limited to 4 hours by default and requires immediate incident postmortem that documents why the standard flow could not be used.

- Privilege Classification (examples):
  - Public: documentation, marketing materials.
  - Internal: non-sensitive product logs, internal dashboards.
  - Confidential: customer metadata, PII derivatives.
  - Restricted: private customer data, keys, secrets, or regulatory data (PCI/PHI).

2) Change Management Patterns
- Principle: low friction for routine safe changes, strong controls for risk-bearing operations.
- Change categories and required controls:
  - Routine (low risk): infra config changes with automated tests and can be deployed with standard CI gating. Requires owner signoff.
  - Scoped (medium risk): schema migrations, model rollouts, config that changes runtime behavior. Requires written change ticket, canary plan, and one peer review.
  - High impact (high risk): database drops, network changes, security policy changes. Requires change advisory board (CAB) approval, rollback plan, and at least one business stakeholder signoff.

- Standard change ticket template (fields to capture):
  - Change summary
  - Owner and rollback owner
  - Risk classification
  - Test plan & acceptance criteria
  - Canary/rollout plan and metrics to monitor
  - Backout/rollback procedure
  - Business impact window and communication plan

- Change Windows and Freeze Periods:
  - Regular maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for low-risk infra work.
  - Freeze windows: critical product launches and major customer migrations as communicated by Product.

- Emergency changes:
  - Must be logged in the Change System with label EMERGENCY, include immediate owner, and require post-change review within 72 hours.

3) Data Management & Handling
- Principle: data minimization, clear ownership, and traceability for sensitive assets.
- Data Inventory: teams must maintain a short inventory (CSV or internal catalog entry) listing datasets, owners, retention, classification, and approved storage locations.

- Retention and Deletion:
  - Default retention for Internal data: 2 years.
  - Confidential data: retention as required by contract or regulation; deletion on request where contractually permitted.
  - Logs: aggregated logs kept for 90 days for operational use, 365 days for audit-critical events.

- Access to Sensitive Data:
  - Sensitive datasets require RBAC gating and an approved Data Access Agreement (DAA).
  - DAA must include purpose, TTL, sampling plan (if applicable), and privacy controls.

- Data Movement Controls:
  - Export of Confidential/Restricted data outside approved VPCs or systems requires Data Security approval and a signed data transfer agreement.

4) Procurement & Expenses (Quick Patterns and Thresholds)
- Principle: reduce operational friction while ensuring spend oversight and supplier risk assessment.
- Approval thresholds (examples):
  - Expense card charges <= $500: personal manager approval.
  - One-off vendor spend <= $5,000: team lead approval + Finance notification.
  - Contracts/POs between $5,000 and $50,000: Finance & Legal review required before signature.
  - > $50,000: Finance, Legal, and VP-level approval; procurement runs RFP if competitive sourcing is required.

- Purchase flow (recommended pattern):
  1. Raise an Intent (short form) in Procurement Portal describing need and budget code.
  2. Obtain team lead approval and attach at least one vendor quote (where possible).
  3. Finance verifies budget and routes to Legal if contract required.
  4. Procurement issues PO and records vendor in the Vendor Registry.

- Expense reporting: receipts required for all business expenses. Card reconciliations must be performed weekly by card owners; managers should spot-check monthly.

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding Patterns
- Principle: consistent supplier risk assessment and secure integration patterns.
- Vendor Risk Triage matrix (quick guide):
  - Low: SaaS tools with no company data, public endpoints only.
  - Medium: tools that store internal documents or telemetry.
  - High: vendors processing customer data, secrets, or requiring network access.

- Onboarding checklist (minimum):
  1. Vendor profile in Vendor Registry (legal name, contacts, service description).
  2. Risk classification and data access assessment.
  3. Security questionnaire for Medium/High vendors; technical assessment for integrations.
  4. Contract with appropriate SLAs, data processing addenda (DPA), and termination rights.
  5. Kickoff documentation including escalation contacts and support SLAs.

- Periodic review: High-risk vendors reviewed annually, Medium every 24 months, Low on significant change.

6) Travel & Business Expense Policy (Practical Patterns)
- Principle: safe, reasonably economical travel while maintaining duty of care.
- Booking guidance: book flights at least 14 days in advance when practical; economy/business split per job level and trip duration as defined in the Travel Allowance Table (below).

  Travel Allowance Table (example):
  | Role band | Flight class guideline | Hotel star range | Per diem (USD/day) |
  | IC1–IC3 | Economy | 3–4 | $75 |
  | IC4–IC5 | Premium economy | 4 | $100 |
  | Leadership | Business for >8hr flights | 4–5 | $150 |

- Approval flow for travel with spend > $2,000 or international travel:
  1. Traveller submits Travel Request with itinerary, purpose, and estimated costs.
  2. Manager approves and confirms budget.
  3. People Ops verifies duty of care advisories (visas, health) and issues travel booking assistance if needed.

- Expense submission timelines: submit within 30 days of expense; exceptions require manager note. Reimbursements processed within payroll cycle following approval.

7) Templates and Operational Primitives (copy & adapt)
- Included templates (canonical forms teams should copy):
  - Access Request template (fields: requestor, role, resources, TTL, justification)
  - Change ticket template (fields listed above)
  - Vendor onboarding checklist (stepwise with owners)
  - Travel request form (itinerary, cost estimate, approvals)
  - DAA stub (purpose, TTL, data types, storage locations)

- Small code snippet: sample CLI to create an access request (internal tool):
  $ infractl access request --role "Engineers/read-only" --resources "prod-cluster" --ttl 30d --reason "Investigating latency"

- Example minimal DAA JSON (text):
  {"dataset": "customer-usage-aggregates", "purpose": "model-training: churn-prediction", "ttl_days": "90", "owner": "team-data-platform@redwood.ai"}

8) Exceptions and Policy Deviations
- Exceptions must be recorded in the Exceptions Register with: owner, scope, approval chain, compensating controls, and an expiration date.
- Short-term operational exceptions (<30 days) can be approved by People Ops + Security; longer-term exceptions require VP-level approval and quarterly reviews.

9) Audit, Metrics, and Continuous Improvement
- Operational metrics to collect (examples):
  - Access request lead time (median approval time).
  - % of temporary access that expired without extension.
  - Change success rate vs. rollback rate.
  - Vendor SLA compliance (uptime, response time).
  - Expense report submission latency.

- Quarterly review: People Ops publishes a short review each quarter with findings, anomalies, and suggested updates. Security and Finance contribute relevant sections.

Appendix: Fast Links and Contacts

- Change System: /internal/change-tracker
- Procurement Portal: /internal/procurement
- Vendor Registry: /internal/vendor-registry
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai

Revision history
- 2024-10-20: Initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2024-12-12: Incorporated Security and Finance comments (Ravi Patel)
- 2025-02-03: Added travel allowances and vendor review cadence (Elena Gomez)

Notes and Next Steps
- Teams should adopt the Role Templates and Change Ticket template within 60 days.
- People Ops will provide a short rollout workshop and Office Hours for adoption questions.
